name: Liquid democracy
summary: Liquid democracy is a hybrid of direct and representative democracy in which every voter may vote on each issue personally or delegate that vote to someone they trust, by topic or across the board. Delegations can be passed on and taken back at any time, so representatives hold power only while they keep voters' confidence. It is a procedural idea, usually put into practice through online platforms, and takes no side on most economic or social questions.
scope: The mainstream strand as developed since the 2000s in Berlin hacker and Pirate-party circles and the LiquidFeedback software (Behrens, Kistner, Nitsche, Swierczek), plus scholarly accounts such as Valsangiacomo's. It treats liquid democracy as a complement to representative institutions, not a revolutionary program. Because it is a decision procedure, most substantive policy statements are answered neutral with low confidence.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The ideology prescribes how collective decisions are made, not whether markets or governments should allocate resources.

public-ownership.rationale: Whether industries are public is left to what delegated and direct votes decide; adherents range across the spectrum.

unions-good.rationale: Nothing in the model concerns labor organization; users come from tech, Pirate and civic circles with mixed views.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare levels are outcomes of whatever majorities choose, not a commitment of the model.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Drug policy is outside the model's concerns; Pirate-party adherents lean liberal but the method itself is neutral.

strong-leader.rationale: The model puts issues rather than leaders at the centre and spreads power through revocable delegations, which is opposed to a leader bypassing gridlock.

state-harmful.rationale: Liquid democracy is a way of running collective decision-making and assumes public institutions exist to be steered by voters; it is not anti-state.

empower-police-military.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is not about military spending, which this statement now asks about alone.

reviewHistory.rationale: Security funding is substantive policy the procedure does not settle.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is not about military spending, which this statement now asks about alone.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

gradual-change.rationale: Adherents typically want institutions made more flexible and responsive, and mostly aim to supplement elections rather than overthrow them; slightly against deference to established forms.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration levels are substantive policy the procedure leaves open.

revolution-justified.rationale: LiquidFeedback's authors present it as a complement to existing representative democracy, working within institutions, so revolution is not part of the approach.

experts-over-public.rationale: Topic-specific delegation lets voters hand decisions to experts they choose, but experts have no built-in extra say and each citizen may override; adherents stress both.

land-value-tax.rationale: A specific tax policy with no link to the sources.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inheritance taxation is a revenue choice voters would settle; the sources attach no tax stance to liquid democracy.

basic-income.rationale: Some Pirate-party members support it but the model does not, so it is left neutral.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Valsangiacomo describes liquid democracy as putting parties and interest groups on a level footing under individual citizen choice, not placing state-recognised bodies at the centre of decisions.

one-party-rule.rationale: The model depends on open competition among delegates, parties and groups, with every voter free to withdraw support, which rules out a single guiding party.

democracy-best.rationale: Liquid democracy is offered as a better form of democracy, so adherents back democracy; the worry about voters choosing badly is the one liquid advocates address through delegation to those who know better.

direct-votes.rationale: Voters can always vote directly on any issue and override a delegate, but the model also keeps delegation, so it is a hybrid rather than direct voting instead of representatives.

natural-rulers.rationale: The model rests on equal votes with trust conferred by voters and revocable at any time, rather than any class born fitter to rule; Valsangiacomo calls it anti-elitist.

war-builds-character.rationale: Nothing in the model glorifies war; an inference from its deliberative, participatory orientation.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The model equalises voting influence in principle, but takes no position on equality of outcomes.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Advocates favour technology for governance, but nothing says to speed change generally despite disruption.

direct-action.rationale: The model is meant to work through votes and complement elections rather than replace them with direct action.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The model is a digital-age institution and has no link to primitivism.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Topic-specific delegation relies on specialised trust, which presupposes people have different areas of expertise.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Rule by one class over another conflicts with equal votes for all and revocable delegation.

collective-farming.rationale: Farm organisation is an economic policy question the model does not decide.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about imperialism, and the statement now asks only whether capitalism inevitably causes wars between great powers.

reviewHistory.rationale: A theory of imperialism that the sources on liquid democracy do not touch.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about imperialism, and the statement now asks only whether capitalism inevitably causes wars between great powers.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

exit-over-voice.rationale: The model is built on voice: more ways to vote and to take back delegations, and nothing treats exit as a stronger check.

organic-representation.rationale: Valsangiacomo says liquid democracy lets citizens choose proxies across topics and puts parties on an equal footing with other groups; fixed family or trade-body representation is not the model.

total-state.rationale: The model distributes decision power among voters and revocable delegates, contrary to a state directing all life.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Delegations are revocable at any time and conditional on trust, the opposite of binding personal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Bound labor contradicts the equal-citizen premise of the model.

single-common-good.rationale: The model aggregates differing preferences issue by issue and lets groups compete on a level field, as Valsangiacomo describes, rather than discovering one common good.

workplace-democracy.rationale: LiquidFeedback is designed for any organisation, and Bollier's summary says it democratises decisions in organisations; the sources do not endorse worker control of large companies specifically.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education funding design is a policy matter the voters decide, not a commitment of the model.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare eligibility is a policy outcome the model does not decide.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Equal participation of all voters is basic to the model, which conflicts with racial classification in law.

state-class-instrument.rationale: A Marxist theory of the state, absent from the sources on liquid democracy.

proportional-representation.rationale: Valsangiacomo argues liquid democracy supports strong proportionality, with voters' choices tracked by weighted proxies.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Wikipedia says liquid democracy arose from political disillusionment, and founders stress elected leaders ignoring the public, though corruption itself is not their claim.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Coercive eugenics conflicts with the model's equal-rights premise.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Transitional-justice policy is not covered; accountability of representatives is a theme but not this question.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The proper scope of government is not set by the model, which only governs how its decisions are made.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A debate internal to Marxism, which the sources do not touch.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A religiously linked policy question the model leaves to voters.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist state doctrine unrelated to the model.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Delegations rest on the voter's conditional trust and can be withdrawn at any time, which expresses consent in a continuous form.

vanguard-party.rationale: A disciplined party leading the people conflicts with the model's emphasis on citizens choosing and recalling their own proxies.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Distributive priorities are a policy matter the model leaves to voters.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Liquid democracy chooses representatives by voluntary delegation, which is a selection model; Landemore-style sortition is a different proposal, so adherents are mostly against replacing elections by lot.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price regulation in emergencies is a policy choice left to voters.

party-controls-media.rationale: The founders treat transparency and open discussion as central, which is incompatible with party control of information.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Delegates in the model are unpaid volunteers with no fixed office, but the sources do not take a position on pay.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Valsangiacomo notes a trade-off between liquid proxies' independence and party discipline, and delegates there act on their own convictions.

clerical-rule.rationale: Authority in the model derives from voters, not from clerics.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The model has no fixed terms; delegates serve while they hold trust, so term limits are not the relevant check.

recall-officials.rationale: Revocability at any time is a defining feature; Wikipedia calls recall central and Valsangiacomo discusses instant recall as the voter's last resort.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Alliance policy is a foreign-policy matter the model does not decide.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: A cultural-moral claim unrelated to the model.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: A populist claim about graduates that the sources do not make, even though the model grew from distrust of political elites.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Curriculum content is a policy outcome the model does not decide.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: A Millian social-liberty claim that the sources do not make.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Liquid democracy has no head of state in its design; some adherents favour direct election, others dispersed delegation, so it is genuinely open.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A debate on Soviet history that the sources do not touch.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Divine or hereditary sanctity of a ruler contradicts authority resting on revocable voter delegation.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: A ruler unbound by law is the opposite of the accountability that revocable delegation builds in.

leader-cult.rationale: Founders put issues rather than leaders at the centre of politics, and a leader cult contradicts that.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist doctrinal question the sources do not touch.

land-redistribution.rationale: Land reform is a substantive policy the model leaves to voters.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Liquid democracy emphasises majority input and revocable proxies, but the sources do not oppose judicial review and Valsangiacomo discusses minority and fragmentation risks, so only a mild lean.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarkic bloc economics is unrelated to the model.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The founders present the tool as a complement to representative democracy, working peacefully through institutions.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Rule by one society over another without consent is contrary to authority resting on voters' delegation.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: An economic-theory question the sources do not touch.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist theory the sources do not touch.

elective-rulers.rationale: Choice of those who hold power by the people, revocable at any time, is the core principle, though the model goes beyond periodic elections.

minority-veto.rationale: Bollier's summary stresses majority preference as the signal and a design for protecting minorities from noise, not a veto over decisions.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The model blurs the parliament-citizen line by letting voters decide directly, so the question has no clean answer in the sources.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Liquid democracy depends on citizens engaging, directly or through chosen proxies; Wikipedia notes few citizens staying active as a weakness.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Political authority in the model rests on voters and recallable delegates, not on a military guardian.

filial-duty.rationale: A family-ethics claim unrelated to the model.

office-by-exam.rationale: Valsangiacomo says proxies are chosen by voters' trust, not by credentials, though topic-specific delegation lets expertise count in practice.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its value turns on whether representatives must follow binding instructions, and the statement now asks only whether voters can recall them at any time.

reviewHistory.rationale: Removal at any time is central, but Valsangiacomo describes proxies as acting on their own convictions, not mandated, so only partially agreed.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its value turns on whether representatives must follow binding instructions, and the statement now asks only whether voters can recall them at any time.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is a policy matter the model leaves to voters.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: A cultural-economic claim the sources do not make.

corporate-influence.rationale: Valsangiacomo warns of interest-group pressure and oligarchic risk, and Wikipedia notes wealthy actors might dominate delegations; the founders' critique of representative politics supports mild agreement.

informal-organisation.rationale: Liquid democracy gives formal, tracked delegation and structured decision procedures to groups, not informal trust-based circles; Pirate parties used it in formal organisations.

religion-illusion.rationale: A claim about religion that the sources do not make.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Small communal society is not part of the model, which has been used in large parties and municipalities, but also not opposed.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The model needs open competition among proxies and open discussion, and suppression would defeat it.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Governing territories for another's benefit without their voters conflicts with authority resting on those governed.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A religious-legal obligation unrelated to the model.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Wikipedia and sources describe a procedural idea that can be used from any position, but do not declare left-right outdated.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist concept the sources do not engage.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Authority comes from voters' delegations in the model, not from God.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inherited office contradicts authority resting on voters' revocable trust.

reification.rationale: A Marxist critical concept the sources do not engage.

racial-franchise.rationale: Equal participation for every voter is basic: each citizen has one vote and may vote directly or delegate; Valsangiacomo links the model to descriptive representation, not to restriction.

online-participation.rationale: The model is realised through online platforms such as LiquidFeedback, and Wikipedia traces it to Berlin hacker culture; the founders call it a concrete instantiation of liquid democracy.

open-government-data.rationale: Founders insist on public, verifiable votes and tracking of proposals, and Wikipedia says voters can see what happened to delegated votes; publication of all government records is a natural extension.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Valsangiacomo and Wikipedia warn of power concentrating among the wealthy in delegation networks, but the claim here is about wealth in general, which the sources do not make.

vote-delegation.rationale: Topic-specific, revocable delegation is the defining mechanism of liquid democracy.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: A procedural idea with no stance on religious institutions; Pirate-party and civic users hold varied views.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The model is neutral on economic systems; users range from socialists to liberals.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Which services are public is a question voters would decide through the system, not one the model answers.

second-chamber.rationale: Sources treat liquid democracy as a complement to representative bodies without taking a view on bicameralism; some proposals even use delegation to fill a chamber.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Delegation resembles bottom-up coordination, but sources describe it as a voting method and do not prescribe confederal structures.

family-wage.rationale: Wage policy is a substantive question the procedure leaves to voters.

person-over-state.rationale: Letting each voter decide directly or revoke a delegation at any time reflects individual agency over institutions, an inference from the design rather than a stated principle.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The model is about delegation of votes, not the constitutional relation between national and regional bodies.

gm-crops.rationale: Agricultural technology is a policy outcome the model leaves to voters.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban planning is a policy outcome the model leaves to voters.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Environmental policy tools are left to what delegated and direct votes decide; the sources take no side.

future-generations.rationale: The model includes no duty to the unborn, who cannot vote or delegate, and adherents hold mixed views; sources are silent.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value rests on women's distinct roles, giving their values more weight, a claim about innate nature or no stated position, and the statement now asks only whether women tend to be more compassionate than men.

reviewHistory.rationale: Nothing in the model concerns gender; adherents hold varied views.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value rests on women's distinct roles, giving their values more weight, a claim about innate nature or no stated position, and the statement now asks only whether women tend to be more compassionate than men.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The sources take no position on military obedience; users hold varied views.

farm-price-support.rationale: It is a procedure that lets voters decide such policies, not a stance on them.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: The procedure itself takes no side on defence policy; users hold varied views.

workers-own-party.rationale: The idea is organisationally neutral and used by parties and groups across the spectrum.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Whether harms are handled by courts or agencies is left to the voters under the procedure.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Sentencing policy is a substantive matter the procedure does not settle.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: A decision procedure takes no side on church-state questions; adherents are split and the sources are silent.

premarital-sex.rationale: A social-morality question that the procedural idea does not address, and Pirate-party users hold varied views.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: It is a decision procedure; users would decide such questions by vote.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: It is a decision procedure with no religious content.

indirect-election.rationale: Its core idea is that each voter votes directly or delegates revocably, rather than higher offices being filled through fixed layers of delegates.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Direct voting or delegation to any trusted person lets voters route around party gatekeepers, though liquid democracy is meant to complement representative institutions and has no leader at its centre.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Welfare levels are outcomes of whatever majorities choose, not a commitment of the model. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: Citizens should be able to delegate their vote on each policy area to someone they trust and withdraw that delegation at any time.
missingStatements.rationale: Topic-specific, revocable delegation is the defining mechanism of liquid democracy, and no current statement asks about delegating votes.

missingStatements.text: Votes on public decisions should be open and verifiable by anyone rather than secret.
missingStatements.rationale: LiquidFeedback's founders reject secret electronic ballots because verifiable open voting guards against fraud, a design choice most democratic theory disputes.
missingStatements.declined: Open, non-secret voting is a LiquidFeedback design choice specific to this one ideology; not worth a bank slot.

notes: Liquid democracy is mostly a procedural idea, so about two thirds of the answers are neutral, low-confidence ones; adherents who are Pirate-party members tend to be liberal on civil liberties, but no source states this. Valsangiacomo notes proxies act on their own convictions rather than as mandated delegates, which is why the recallable-delegates answer is only +1.
